purpose: This medication is a birth control patch that helps prevent pregnancy. It is worn on the skin and releases hormones continuously into your body. It may also help make your periods more regular and reduce menstrual cramps.
how_it_works: The patch contains two hormones — a progestin and an estrogen — that are absorbed through your skin into your bloodstream. These hormones work together to stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix, making it harder for sperm to reach an egg.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include skin irritation or redness where you apply the patch, nausea, breast tenderness or soreness, headaches, mood changes, spotting or breakthrough bleeding between periods, and decreased sex drive. These often improve after the first few months.
warnings: Do not use this patch if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as this raises the risk of serious heart problems like blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. This patch does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Seek medical help right away if you have severe chest pain, leg pain, trouble breathing, or vision changes.
typical_dosing: You apply one patch to clean, dry skin on your belly, upper arm, back, or buttocks once a week for three weeks in a row. Then you go patch-free for one week — this is when your period usually comes. After that patch-free week, you start a new patch and repeat the cycle. Always change your patch on the same day each week.
